stem: A facility changes water sources and laboratory data show the new source contributes substantially different mineral content. What is the best nutrition response?
choices: Keep the fertilizer recipe unchanged but recalculate irrigation volume, because source-water minerals primarily affect water demand rather than the nutrient composition of the finished solution
Account for the new source-water contribution when evaluating the complete nutrient program instead of assuming the old recipe produces the same final chemistry
Increase every fertilizer concentrate by the same percentage to maintain the previous fertilizer-to-water ratio without separately accounting for ions already present in the new source
Adjust the source-water pH to the facility's previous value and assume that matching pH restores the prior mineral profile of the finished nutrient solution
rationale: Source water can contribute dissolved minerals and alter the starting ionic load. Nutrient programs should be evaluated as a complete system that includes source-water chemistry.
